issues.legal_issue: A complainant may seek special leave to appeal from an acquittal recorded in the complainant’s separately instituted case even when that case is tried jointly with a police-report case.
material_facts: Police filed a charge-sheet against two accused, while the complainant separately filed a complaint charging those accused and a third accused.
The cases retained separate numbers, were committed separately, and were tried together.
The court recorded acquittals separately in each case; the police had not charged the third accused.
The complainant applied for special leave to appeal against the acquittals.
issues.conclusion: The complainant was entitled to have the special-leave petition considered in respect of the complaint case, and the matter was remitted to the High Court for that consideration. The Court left to the High Court whether any appeal could extend beyond the third accused.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 417(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, a complainant may appeal from an acquittal if the acquittal was recorded in a case instituted upon that complaint and the High Court grants special leave. Sections 4(1)(h) and 190 distinguish a complaint from a police report and identify complaint-based cognizance. The separate identity of the complaint case was maintained despite joint trial, so there was no merger that defeated the statutory right. Sections 417(4) and 417(5) address the time for applying and the effect of refusal of special leave. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: complainant_seeks_special_leave_after_acquittal and complaint_instituted_case and acquittal_recorded_in_complaint_case and separate_case_identity_maintained

predicates.complainant_seeks_special_leave_after_ac: A complainant applies for special leave to appeal after an acquittal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.complaint_instituted_case: The complainant instituted a distinct criminal case by making a complaint alleging an offence.
predicates.acquittal_recorded_in_complaint_case: The acquittal was recorded in the case instituted by the complainant’s complaint.
predicates.separate_case_identity_maintained: The complaint case retained its separate identity through the proceedings, including when tried jointly with another case.

issues.definition: When a complainant seeks special leave after an acquittal in a distinct complaint case whose identity remained separate, the complainant is entitled to have the special-leave petition heard.

issues.legal_issue: An unsuccessful revision does not extinguish a complainant’s statutory right to seek special leave to appeal from an acquittal in a complaint case.
material_facts: The complainant applied for revision after the High Court dismissed the special-leave petition, and the revision application was rejected.
The complainant also sought special leave to challenge the rejection of the revision, but that request was refused.
The complainant’s original special-leave application concerned an acquittal recorded in a separately instituted complaint case.
issues.conclusion: The revision proceedings and their outcome did not bar or conclude the complainant’s statutory right to have the original special-leave petition heard.
issues.legal_principle: Section 417(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 confers on a complainant the right to apply for special leave where an acquittal is recorded in a case instituted upon the complaint. The Court held that pursuing revision, and the result of that revision, did not cause that statutory right to be lost. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.complainant_seeks_special_leave_after_ac: A complainant applies for special leave to appeal after an acquittal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.complaint_instituted_case: The acquittal concerns a criminal case instituted by the complainant’s complaint.
predicates.revision_application_rejected: The complainant pursued revision concerning the acquittal or related order, and the revision application was rejected.

issues.definition: If a complainant seeks special leave concerning an acquittal in a complaint case after an unsuccessful revision, the right to seek special leave remains.
